title: Measuring cold-storage temperatures under Board guidance, temperature logs, one-year records and the food and beverage bar
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.22(3), a pharmacy shall measure and maintain refrigerator and freezer temperatures in accordance with Board guidance. Under 247 CMR 9.22(4), a pharmacy shall maintain temperature logs to clearly identify out of range temperatures and shall document actions taken in response to an out of range temperature, and shall maintain records for at least one year. Under 247 CMR 9.22(5), a pharmacy may not store any food or beverage in a refrigerator or freezer used to store medications.
exam_relevance: Tests the monitoring and recordkeeping half of 247 CMR 9.22: temperatures kept in accordance with Board guidance, logs that make excursions visible, documentation of the response, a one-year record, and the ban on food or beverage in a medication unit.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.fact: minimum retention of refrigerator and freezer temperature records

common_confusions: The regulation itself states no temperature range or checking frequency; it requires temperatures to be measured and maintained in accordance with Board guidance.
Logging an out of range temperature is not enough; actions taken in response must also be documented.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's publication of 247 CMR 9.00 on mass.gov (PDF, Mass. Register #1536, 12/6/2024).
